original_value: Neuroinflammation is a common factor in neurodegenerative diseases, and it has been demonstrated that galectin-3 activates microglia and astrocytes, leading to inflammation. This means that inhibition of galectin-3 may become a new strategy for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases. Based on this motivation, the objective of this study is to explore an integrated new approach for finding lead compounds that inhibit galectin-3, by combining universal artificial intelligence algorithms with traditional drug screening methods. Based on molecular docking method, potential compounds with high binding affinity were screened out from Chinese medicine database. Manifold artificial intelligence algorithms were performed to validate the docking results and further screen compounds. Among all involved predictive methods, the deep learning-based algorithm made 500 modeling attempts, and the square correlation coefficient of the best trained model on the test sets was 0.9. The XGBoost model reached a square correlation coefficient of 0.97 and a mean square error of only 0.01. We switched to the ZINC database and performed the same experiment, the results showed that the compounds in the former database showed stronger affinity. Finally, we further verified through molecular dynamics simulation that the complex composed of the candidate ligand and the target protein showed stable binding within 100 ns of simulation time. In summary, combined with the application based on artificial intelligence algorithms, we unearthed the active ingredients 1,2-Dimethylbenzene and Typhic acid contained in Crataegus pinnatifida and Typha angustata might be the effective inhibitors of neurodegenerative diseases. The high prediction accuracy of the models shows that it has practical application value on small sample data sets such as drug screening.

result.paraphrase: Neuroinflammation is a common feature of neurodegenerative diseases, and galectin-3 has been shown to activate microglia and astrocytes, thereby inducing inflammation. Accordingly, inhibiting galectin-3 may offer a new therapeutic strategy for neurodegenerative diseases. Motivated by this, the study aimed to develop an integrated approach for identifying lead compounds that inhibit galectin-3 by combining general artificial intelligence algorithms with conventional drug screening methods. Using molecular docking, candidate compounds with high binding affinity were selected from a Chinese medicine database. Multiple AI algorithms were then applied to validate the docking findings and further filter compounds. Among the predictive methods used, the deep learning algorithm made 500 modeling attempts, and its best model achieved a test-set square correlation coefficient of 0.9. The XGBoost model achieved a square correlation coefficient of 0.97 and a mean squared error of just 0.01. The same experiment was then carried out using the ZINC database, and the results indicated that compounds from the former database had stronger affinity. Finally, molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that the complex formed by the candidate ligand and target protein remained stably bound over 100 ns of simulation time. In summary, with the support of AI-based methods, the active ingredients 1,2-Dimethylbenzene and Typhic acid from Crataegus pinnatifida and Typha angustata were identified as potential effective inhibitors of neurodegenerative diseases. The models’ high prediction accuracy demonstrates practical value for small-sample tasks such as drug screening.
